claims.text: Large language models (LLMs) excel at numerical estimation.
Large language models (LLMs) struggle to correctly quantify uncertainty.
Large language models (LLMs) are systematically overconfident when constructing confidence intervals around their own answers.
FermiEval is a benchmark of Fermi-style estimation questions with a rigorous scoring rule for confidence interval coverage and sharpness.
Across several modern models, nominal 99% intervals cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average.
A conformal prediction based approach that adjusts the intervals obtains accurate 99% observed coverage.
A conformal prediction based approach reduces the Winkler interval score by 54%.
Direct log-probability elicitation methods reduce overconfidence at high confidence levels.
Quantile adjustment methods reduce overconfidence at high confidence levels.
The perception-tunnel theory explains why LLMs exhibit overconfidence.
When reasoning under uncertainty, LLMs act as if sampling from a truncated region of their inferred distribution, neglecting its tails.
